title: npm 11 drops a bin path written with ./
body: Write bin paths without a leading ./ ("src/cli.js"). Before publishing, read package.json out of the packed tarball (npm pack, then tar --force-local -xOf) to confirm bin survived, and watch for "npm auto-corrected some errors" in npm publish output; .github/scripts/check-pack.mjs fails CI on a ./ bin path, and this memory's check says so at the edit. Why: npm 11.6 removed "./src/cli.js" as an invalid script name at publish time, only as a warning, which would have shipped the package without its deltadictum command and broken the Codex install.
not_derivable: npm removes the path with a warning only; nothing fails until the published package lacks its command.

check.say: npm 11 drops a bin path written with ./ at publish time: write it as "src/cli.js".

evidence.summary: CI refuses a bin path starting with ./.
